decisions.reason: As a flagship product line tightly tied to the core dental software business and the firm's digital direction, it likely meets or stays close enough to aspiration levels that a growing firm with R&D and slack would continue to support it.

The remote support tool is a low-distance complement to the established software and service offer, so even with modest results its synergies and limited maintenance burden make continued retention more likely than withdrawal.

The analytics dashboard fits the move toward more connected and efficiently managed practices, and unless performance is clearly below aspiration management would keep it while learning and refining the offer.

A complete practice bundle is very close to the firm's established offer and can leverage existing sales, support, and integration resources, so behavioral search pressures to drop it are relatively weak.

The job and practice listing portal is the most distant from the firm's core capabilities and customer workflow software, so if its results fall short of aspiration it is the likeliest candidate for problemistic resource reallocation to the core business and new development.
